newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania moves to ratify key treaty with Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Romania moves to ratify key treaty with Ukraine.

text.p: Romania took a first step on Thursday towards endorsing a key treaty settling old rifts over borders and minorities with neighbouring formerly Soviet Ukraine.
Parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies voted 165-92 to ratify the pact signed earlier this month by reformist President Emil Constantinescu and Ukraine President Leonid Kuchma.
Romania's leftists, who lost their seven-year grip on power in 1996 elections, voted against the treaty as did nationalists, now a small minority in a parliament dominated by centrists.
Before taking effect, the pact has to go through the upper house Senate, where centrists also have a comfortable majority.

"This treaty has brought great security benefits to Romania and has ... advantages to the Romanian minority in Ukraine," Constantinescu told a news conference on Thursday, marking his first 200 days in power since he ousted an ex-communist in last November's elections.

Constantinescu will meet Kuchma and Moldovan President Petru Lucinschi in Ukraine's Danube river port of Izmail next week to discuss plans to boost economic ties and set up a free trade zone between the three ex-communist neighbours.
Bucharest dropped its previous insistence that Kiev should atone in the treaty text for the 1939 Soviet-Nazi pact under which Moscow annexed Romanian lands now part of modern Ukraine.

Negotiators have agreed to leave unsolved issues -- including definition of Black Sea borders in areas which both countries believe are rich in oil and gas deposits -- to be settled as part of separate accords.

Romania signed a similar deal patching rifts with its former rival Hungary last year in a bid to boost its chances of getting invited to join NATO, alongside favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, when the alliance announces its first eastward expansion at a July 8-9 summit in Madrid.
